prompt: Which observation in the Geiger–Marsden–Rutherford experiment shows that the nucleus contains most of the mass of the atom?
options: Most alpha particles passed straight through
A few alpha particles were deflected through very large angles
Alpha particles were absorbed by the foil
markscheme: **B.** Only a massive concentrated object can reverse a fast alpha particle.

prompt: An atom has four energy levels. What is the maximum number of different wavelengths it can emit?
markscheme: **C.** Each pair of levels gives one line: $\tfrac{4\times3}{2} = 6$.

prompt: Nucleus X has nucleon number $A$ and nucleus Y has nucleon number $8A$. What is $\tfrac{\text{radius of Y}}{\text{radius of X}}$ and $\tfrac{\text{density of Y}}{\text{density of X}}$?
markscheme: **A.** $R \propto A^{1/3}$, so the radius doubles; mass and volume both scale with $A$, so density is unchanged.

prompt:
The energy levels of hydrogen are given by $E_n = -\tfrac{13.6}{n^2}\ \text{eV}$.

**(a)** Explain why the energies are negative. **[1]**

**(b)** Calculate the wavelength of the photon emitted in the transition from $n = 4$ to $n = 2$ and state the region of the spectrum. **[3]**

**(c)** Outline how the Bohr model accounts for the existence of discrete energy levels. **[2]**
markscheme:
**(a)** Zero energy is defined for a free (unbound) electron; energy must be supplied to free a bound electron ✓

**(b)** $\Delta E = 3.40 - 0.85 = 2.55\ \text{eV} = 4.08\times10^{-19}\ \text{J}$ ✓; $\lambda = \tfrac{hc}{\Delta E} = \tfrac{6.63\times10^{-34}\times3.00\times10^8}{4.08\times10^{-19}} = 4.9\times10^{-7}\ \text{m}$ ✓; visible (blue-green) ✓

**(c)** Angular momentum is quantised, $mvr = \tfrac{nh}{2\pi}$ ✓; combined with the electric force providing the centripetal force this allows only certain radii and therefore certain energies ✓
